title: Father's drumming and refusing to cut two men to play the Orpheum circuit
summary: His father also played drums, and in Minneapolis he turned down the Orpheum circuit rather than cut two players from his 11-piece band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You mentioned a great long string of instruments that your father played, but you never mentioned drums. Was that just an omission, or ...
Well, that was an omission, because I saw him play drums, too.
I figured that -- well, he taught you, right?
Yeah, uh huh. But I saw him play drums, too.
Okay. Do you know of any of the people who were in your father's band? I mean do you remember any names?

No. See ... no. Because the thing, the band that I think that was probably the best band was in Minneapolis, where he had a chance to go on the Orpheum circuit, I think, but he had 11 pieces and they were gonna take the band and myself, you know, in front of the band, and Lester and Irma.

But they wanted him to cut 2 men out of the band, you know, and he was a high principled man and he would not. And everybody was just dying to get on the Orpheum circuit, you know, that was the biggest thing that you could do in

Vaudeville then. But he wouldn't -- I remember that he would not cut 2 guys from the band, and so they continued to do those little one nighters up in Bismarck, North Dakota, you know, Devils Lake -- they used to play all over the Dakotas, but I don't think there were any 'name' people that we would know, you know, up in Minneapolis way.
